criteria.name: voice_authenticity
criteria.description: Each character has a distinct voice that sounds like a real person, not a walking theme or archetype. Distinctness comes from how they think and what they reach for under pressure — not just vocabulary. Lines vary in length and register within a character. Test: if you can predict every line a character will say from knowing their one defining trait, score 0–35. If characters are distinct but feel like symbols rather than people, score 30–55. If characters are distinct AND feel capable of going off-script when emotional, score 70+.

criteria.name: turn_responsiveness
criteria.description: Each line responds to what was just said — reacts, builds on, or pushes back against the specific previous line. The conversation has momentum. Test: could the line appear anywhere else in the scene without losing meaning? If yes across most lines, score 0–40. If characters are delivering parallel monologues that happen to alternate, score 0–30.

criteria.name: dramatic_payoff
criteria.description: Each scene accomplishes something — emotional state shifts, a revelation lands, the relationship changes in some legible way. No character states the theme or their emotional state plainly. Test: if the scene ends in the same emotional place it began, score 0–40. If a character explains the meaning out loud ('I realize now that...'), score 0–35 regardless of other qualities.

criteria.name: subtext
criteria.description: Meaning lives in implication, deflection, or what goes unsaid — not just in what is stated. At least some of the emotional content requires the reader to read between the lines. Test: if every feeling is named and nothing is implied across all scenes, score 0–35.

criteria.name: renpy_correctness
criteria.description: Scripts are valid Ren'Py syntax. Every scene has a label, ends with jump/return, character dialogue uses the correct id (not the name). show/hide/scene statements are present and use valid ids. Test: if any scene is missing its label or ending statement, score 0–50. If character ids in dialogue lines match the define statements, score full marks for this criterion.
